criteria.wording: Population and recruitment: Target population, eligibility, recruitment, and major exclusions are fully reported.
Experimental conditions: Treatment and comparator, or all randomized attributes and levels, are reported precisely enough to reproduce.
Randomization: Unit, probabilities or ratio, sequence-generation process, and restrictions are fully reported.
Outcome measurement: Outcomes, coding, timing, and primary or secondary status are fully reported.
Participant flow: Numbers recruited, randomized, exposed, followed, and analyzed are reported as applicable.
Estimand: The causal or descriptive quantity being estimated is explicitly defined.
Estimator/model: The statistical operation used to estimate the estimand is reconstructable from the text, table, or table notes.
Analysis unit: The reader can determine whether observations are participants, profiles, choices, sessions, or another unit.
Coding and reference categories: Treatment coding, outcome coding, omitted categories, and reference levels are explicit.
Specification: Covariates, fixed effects, weights, transformations, and column-to-column specification changes are explicit.
Dependence and inference: Standard errors, clustering, repeated-observation dependence, bootstrap or permutation procedures, and confidence-interval construction are explicit.
Missingness and attrition: Inclusion rules, missing outcomes, exclusions, attrition, and corresponding adjustments are explicit.
Multiplicity and analysis status: Multiple-testing procedures and prespecified versus exploratory analyses are distinguished.
Analysis sample: The number of observations used in each focal analysis is reported.
Group quantities: Relevant control means, treatment means, marginal means, or other raw quantities are reported.
Effect and uncertainty: Effect estimates and standard errors or confidence intervals are reported.
Model-to-result traceability: Each focal numerical result can be connected directly to a particular outcome, contrast, specification, sample, and inference procedure.
Robustness analyses: Alternative specifications and sensitivity analyses are explained sufficiently to understand what changed.
Internal-validity threats: Attrition, noncompliance, spillovers, demand effects, measurement problems, and other relevant threats are discussed.
Inferential scope: The paper distinguishes the randomized contrast from broader claims about mechanisms, populations, and settings.
